text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- Iraq's foreign minister urges Arab countries to help Iraqi people perform the haj (pilgrimage) to Mecca this year
- Iraq denounces flights by U.S. spy planes over its territory
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright fails to persuade Italian leaders to adhere to American policies
- Egypt says Israel does not want peace with Arabs
- Symposium in House of Commons on sanctions on Iraq and its people
- Ankara uses blackmail in relations with Arabs
- Korean companies open medical fair in Baghdad
- Iraq to hold five specialised exhibitions this year
- First batch of Saddam commandos join military training
- Plans adopted to cultivate every inch of agricultural land in Iraq
- Editorial on the success of economic measures taken by President Saddam Hussein last year
- How Iraq won the 'mother of battles' over Kuwait
- Article says American women face worst conditions in the world
- Iraqi major-general writes about the poor performance of British airforce during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait
JUMHOURIYA
- Egypt accuses Iran of attempts to topple its government
- Editorial openly supports Egypt and Algeria in struggle against Islamic fundamentalists
BABEL
- Editorial calls for the sacking of Rolf Ekeus head of the U.N. Special Commission on Iraq
